rejected.title: BCE, CE and BP
card: BCE
Before the Common Era. These dates are before the year 1. They count down towards it, so 500 BCE is earlier than 200 BCE.
CE
Common Era. These dates are after the year 1. They count up, so 200 CE is earlier than 500 CE.
BP
Before present. Archaeologists use it to count years back from the present, which is set at 1950 CE. A larger BP number means an older date.
BCE and CE are both measured from the year 1. BP is measured back from the present, fixed at 1950.
rejected.remember: BCE counts down to year 1, CE counts up from it, and BP counts back from 1950.

a.q: Which of these dates is the earliest?
a.why: BCE dates count down towards the year 1, so 800 BCE is further back in time than 300 BCE. Both are earlier than any CE date. A student might pick 300 BCE because 300 is a smaller number, but BCE numbers get smaller as time moves forward.
a.clue: BCE numbers get smaller as time moves forward.

b.q: An archaeologist reports that a stone tool found in Queensland is 12,000 years BP. What does BP tell you about this date?
opts: It counts 12,000 years back from the present
It counts 12,000 years forward from the year 1
It counts 12,000 years back from the year 1
It is a CE date, so the tool is fairly recent
b.why: BP means before present, so the date counts 12,000 years back from the present, which archaeologists set at 1950 CE. The tempting answer is counting back from the year 1, but that is how BCE works, and BP is not a CE date either.
b.clue: Think about what the P in BP stands for.

version.title: BCE, CE and BP
card: BCE
Before the Common Era. These dates come before the year 1 CE. They count down towards it, so 500 BCE is earlier than 200 BCE.
CE
Common Era. CE dates start at the year 1 and count up, so 200 CE is earlier than 500 CE. There is no year 0: 1 BCE is followed by 1 CE.
BP
Before present. Archaeologists use it to count years back from the present, which is fixed at 1950 CE. A larger BP number means an older date.
BCE and CE dates are counted from the start of the Common Era. BP dates are counted back from 1950.
version.remember: BCE numbers shrink as time goes on, CE numbers grow, and BP counts back from 1950.

a.q: Put these dates in time order. Which one comes first?
a.why: BCE dates count down towards 1 CE, so 750 BCE is further back in time than 250 BCE, and every BCE date comes before every CE date. 250 BCE is tempting because 250 is a smaller number, but BCE numbers get smaller as time moves forward.
a.clue: In BCE, a bigger number is further back in time.

b.q: A museum label says charcoal from an old campfire is 8,000 years BP. What does this date mean?
opts: The year 8,000 in the Common Era
b.why: BP means before present, and archaeologists fix the present at 1950, so the charcoal is 8,000 years older than 1950. Counting back from the year 1 is how BCE works, not BP.
b.clue: What year do archaeologists treat as the present?
